meta.question: How do we roll out a new feature safely?
meta.title: Rolling out a feature safely
meta.author: Engineering practices guide

answer.headline: Ship the code switched off behind a feature flag, turn it on for staff, then for a small share of users while watching agreed guardrail metrics, and widen in stages, with one switch that turns it off in seconds.
answer.text: Separating deploy from release means a bad feature becomes a flag change rather than an emergency rollback. The stages and guardrails are agreed before the rollout starts, so nobody has to judge under pressure.
points: Deploy is not release: the code goes live switched off
Each stage has a minimum time and a guardrail that stops the rollout automatically
Remove the flag once the feature is fully on, so flags do not pile up

blocks.title: Rollout stages
blocks.caption: Any stage can go back to off if a guardrail is breached.

meta.title: Feature rollout
meta.description: A feature moves from off to everyone in stages; a breach at any stage switches it off.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: Five stages from off to everyone, and one way back.

steps.title: Try it ourselves
steps.description: Staff use the feature for real before any customer sees it.

steps.title: Canary
steps.description: 1% of users; compare their metrics with everyone else's.

steps.title: Widen
steps.description: 25%, then 50%, then everyone, a day at each step.

steps.title: Stop
steps.description: A breached guardrail turns the flag off; investigate before trying again.

items.title: Wrap the feature in a flag
items.text: Default off in every environment. Test both the on and off paths.

items.title: Agree guardrails and owners
items.text: Which metrics, what threshold, who decides. Write them in the release ticket.

items.title: Deploy switched off
items.text: Nothing changes for users; the deploy can go out with other work.

items.title: Enable for staff
items.text: Fix what staff find before any customer sees it.

items.title: Canary at 1%
items.text: Compare the 1% with the rest for at least a full day, including a peak period.

items.title: Widen in steps
items.text: 25%, 50%, 100%. Do not widen on a Friday or before a holiday.

items.title: Clean up
items.text: Remove the flag and the old code path within two sprints.

blocks.title: Example guardrails
rows: More than 0.5 percentage points above control

items.title: No control group
items.text: Without comparing against users who do not have the feature, normal daily swings look like problems, or hide them.

items.title: Flag that cannot turn off
items.text: Database changes made only for the new path can make 'off' unsafe. Keep migrations backwards compatible.

items.title: Flags left forever
items.text: Old flags multiply the code paths nobody tests.

blocks.label: Rule of thumb
blocks.body: If you cannot say in one sentence what would make you switch the feature off, you are not ready to switch it on.

items.title: Feature Toggles (aka Feature Flags), Pete Hodgson on martinfowler.com
